entries.title: Job 37:1
segments: At this; the tempest mentioned in the preceding and following verses.

entries.title: Job 37:2
segments: The noise of his voice; the thunder.

entries.title: Job 37:4
segments:
After it; after the lightning. 
 
  He will not stay them; he will not hold back his lightnings; or, as others prefer, his treasures of rain, hail, and wind.

entries.title: Job 37:5
segments: All the operations of nature are under the control of God.  He orders the seasons and all things with regard to them as seemeth good in his sight; as is best suited to promote his glory and the good of those who trust in him.

entries.title: Job 37:7
segments: He sealeth up the hand; by the approach of the storm he stops the laborer in his work.

entries.title: Job 37:9
segments: The north; the original word seems to mean scattering winds; that is, winds coming from the north, scattering the clouds, and bringing cold weather.

entries.title: Job 37:10
segments: The breadth of the waters is straitened; by being frozen up.

entries.title: Job 37:11
segments: He wearieth the thick cloud; exhausts it, by causing it to pour out its contents of rain upon the earth.  Some prefer to render, Also he ladeth his thick cloud with moisture.

entries.title: Job 37:13
segments:
It; the rain, or storm. 
 
Storms are sometimes sent, and property to a great amount swept away or destroyed, for the correction of those who have sought it as their chief good; to show them the uncertainty of earthly things, and lead them to seek durable riches and righteousness, a treasure in heaven which will never be taken away.

entries.title: Job 37:15
segments: Disposed them; the clouds, rain, thunder, etc.

entries.title: Job 37:16
segments: The balancings of the clouds; see note to

. 
 
As me by doing their duty may enjoy all the benefits of the seasons without being able to explain the reasons of them, so the believer in revelation may have all its benefits without being able to explain its mysteries, or understand the reasons of divine dispensations.

entries.title: Job 37:17
segments: Quieteth the earth by the south wind; by the sultry sirocco, which overpowers every thing by its heat, and produces universal languor.

entries.title: Job 37:19
segments: Him; God, when we think to arraign him for his doings.

entries.title: Job 37:20
segments:
Swallowed up; overwhelmed with the greatness, majesty, and glory of God. 
 
Suitable views of God will always inspire reverence and awe, humility and holy fear, as well as affection, confidence, and joy.

entries.title: Job 37:21
segments: And now--cleanseth them; the meaning, according to our version, is that the bright light of the sun is hid from men's view by the clouds, till the wind cleanses them away.  Some propose to render thus: "And now men cannot look upon the bright light which is in the clouds, when the wind passeth and cleanseth them;" that is, it is too dazzling to behold.

entries.title: Job 37:23
segments: He will not afflict; improperly, or without good reasons.

entries.title: Job 37:24
segments:
Wise of heart; He receives no assistance from the most intelligent; but forms and preserves his own plans, without asking counsel or receiving aid from any of his creatures.

Many suppose that the tempest out of which God soon spoke,
